_meta.note: Built from pilot data. These are not results and must not be quoted as findings. The only pilot-derived numbers the paper may quote are the design.* and mde.* keys (pre-registered detectable gaps, results/mde.json).
_meta.source: rebuilt in memory from pilot logs with analyze.py functions (family entry rule waived)

fig1.caption: Figure 1. Design. Each AI agent acts as the buyer's own shopping agent. It sees an account profile, a request and one page of 8 real products, then asks a question or buys. Only the account name changes between runs; request, page, product order and replies are held fixed. Prices are from the real page hair_shampoo_fine_straight__S. Process adapted from Khaki and Choi (2026), with a one-page store in the style of WebShop (Yao et al. 2022) and ACES (Allouah et al.).

fig2.caption: Figure 2. Average price paid per purchase, S0 (fully specified request, no budget), by name group. Dots: mean over names of the dollar price after removing task, wording and order effects; bars: 95% CI across names (Claude Haiku 5.5: 4 to 5 names per group, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: 4 to 7 names per group). Dashed line: average price of the cheapest product that fit the request, over the tasks in these runs. Descriptive view behind H1 and H2; the tests are in Figure 3. Where a model bought the same product for every name, all groups sit on one value with no interval. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: exploratory. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig3.caption: Figure 3. Confirmatory price tests (Holm across 4 tests). Dots: gap in price paid for the same request, names associated with Black buyers vs White buyers (H1) and women vs men (H2), name-level OLS with HC2 errors; bars: 95% CI. Shaded band: the detectable gap fixed before the main run, 1.4% after Holm; a true gap this size would be flagged at least 80% of the time. Dotted lines: equivalence margin. Dollar amounts translate the percent gap at the reference group's average price (names associated with White buyers for H1, with men for H2); they are not a separate test. Rows below the line are exploratory models: estimates only, in no tested family. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig4.caption: Figure 4. Hair and skin tasks. A to C: vague requests where the buyer's need was hidden and the agent bought without asking. A: share of picks that fit the hidden need. B and C: wrong-product (other need) rate split by the buyer's actual need, never pooled, since a guess from a name hurts buyers whose need does not match the guess and those errors cancel in a pooled number (B and C exploratory). D: with the need stated (S0 and S1), share of identity-linked picks (coily 4C or deep shade), the H3 outcome. Dots: mean over names; bars: 95% CI across names. H4 compares names associated with Black and White buyers in the A to C episodes; its detectable gap after Holm is 11.5 points. H4 conditions on not asking, so the ask rate (Figure 5) belongs beside it. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig5.caption: Figure 5. Share of episodes where the agent asked the buyer a question (top) and where it did not complete a purchase (bottom), by arm and name group; dots: mean over names, bars: 95% CI across names. Exploratory; tests controlled at a 10% false discovery rate, and q is printed only where q < 0.10. No purchase includes refusals, errors, invalid product IDs and no tool call. In V the agent could ask twice before a scripted 'choose one yourself' reply (Deviation D1); runs logged before D1 keep one answered ask. Second-ask rates are in the CSV. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig6.caption: Figure 6. Method checks, run before any group result was examined (PLAN 8). A: a planted 'always buy the lowest-priced product that meets the request' preference, per planted name (lines), S0 vs PB on the same tasks, wordings and orders. B: with the planted names' PB episodes swapped into S0, the frozen H1 test's estimate and 95% CI vs the expected diluted gap (planted shift x 5 / 20); PLAN 8.1 requires the CI to cover it, and detection only when the swapped data's own detectable gap says it should be found. C: arm P, per name, 'best quality' minus 'cheapest that fits' (small marks: names; large mark: mean). D: share of 1,000 label shuffles with p < 0.05 for each confirmatory test (limit 8.5%; above it the test switches to its permutation p-value). PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig7.caption: Figure 7. Gaps by model and outcome (focal group minus comparison group, name level, 95% CI); price in percent, rates in percentage points. Shaded: detectable gap after Holm where pre-registered. Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna are confirmatory when they enter the family (PLAN 3); Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and OLMo 3 7B are exploratory, shown as estimates only. The two right columns are exploratory tests (Benjamini-Hochberg, 10%). One model version per vendor on one date. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA1.caption: Figure A1. Position bias (PLAN 10 Figure A1, same computation as analyze.py). Share of purchases at each displayed position, forward vs reversed product order, arms S0, S1 and V pooled; dashed line: 12.5%, no position preference. The product order is part of every test cell, so position is held fixed by design. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA2.caption: Figure A2. Price paid vs the no-name buyer, by name group and arm (PLAN 10 Figure 1, same computation as analyze.py). Dots: group mean of name averages after removing task, wording and order effects, minus the no-name accounts' mean, as percent; bars: Welch 95% CI across names. Shaded in S0: the detectable gap after Holm. * Hispanic and Asian cells are exploratory. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.
